deviation: The registered adoption rule was met on dev2, so the registration made h16 the main configuration of the paper. On the test sets h16 is worse than sigma on every ImageNet-1K group (intervals of the FPR95 difference above 0), on CIFAR-100 and on ImageNet-200 far-OOD, and better only on the ImageNet-200 near-OOD FPR95 (with a lower AUROC). Following the author's statement made before the runs ('good -> main text, bad -> supplement'), sigma remains the main configuration of the paper and h16 is reported as a registered variant in the appendix (paper v19, Appendix A.13-A.14) with all its values. This is a deviation from the registered adoption rule. It was decided after the test results were read and is disclosed here, in docs/PREREGISTRATION.md and in the paper (Appendix A.12, A.13.4).
notes: dev2 has the construction of dev1 and shares its far-OOD set (OpenImage-O validation list); non-inferiority on dev2 did not carry over to the benchmarks.

The base combination chosen on dev1 (s0 * p) is outside the validity statement; on the benchmarks its x TINS near-OOD value is far worse than sigma x TINS because the floor of p lets the base detector order the unknowns (the same reason the paper multiplies the base detector with sigma).
Nothing was changed in the code or the configuration after the registration; all values are reported.
